A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural dueling-bandit work. Their text, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated methods, proofs and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original synthetic dueling-bandit and binary-feedback simulations, including regret comparisons and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: The synthetic simulations are retained. Appendix F additionally reports an original LLM response-selection experiment using simulated preference feedback.

M1.justification: The neural architectures, cross-entropy objectives and NDB/NCBF UCB and Thompson-sampling selection rules are retained. Appendix F applies the existing algorithms to response embeddings. The new same-arm discussion explains omitting constant-loss observations rather than introducing a different estimator.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic reward-function tasks only. Appendix F adds LLM response optimization using ChatGPT-generated candidates and preferences simulated from a reward model pretrained on Anthropic Helpfulness and Harmlessness data. This substantially extends the evaluated domain, without constituting a human study.

E2.justification: The original synthetic comparator sets are retained, including LinDB-UCB, LinDB-TS and CoLSTIM. The new response-selection comparison adds Random alongside the existing linear variants; Figure 9 confirms their participation.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 50 generated responses per prompt, Sentence-BERT embeddings, reward-model-simulated preferences, and scores calculated as selected-response rewards summed and divided by iterations, reported at multiples of ten. Existing synthetic protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The exploration-parameter, arm-count, feature-dimension and reward-function sensitivity studies are retained unchanged. The LLM experiment adds task evaluation; the new complexity and same-arm passages provide analytical discussion rather than additional ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 repetitions and 95% confidence intervals, and the original uncertainty displays are unchanged. Figure 9 adds shaded bands but specifies no different statistical procedure, seed policy or repetition count.

E6.justification: All original plotted results are retained unchanged. Figure 9 adds response-selection learning curves: NDB-UCB achieves the highest scores, while NDB-TS remains slightly below LinDB-TS. Thus the new evidence does not support the accompanying blanket superiority claim for both neural algorithms.

T1.justification: v2 tightens the stated sublinearity condition from tilde-O(sqrt(T)) to tilde-o(sqrt(T)). Appendix B corrects an equality to an inequality in v1 Eq. (33)/v2 Eq. (31) and supplies its greedy-selection justification. Computational-cost derivations are added. The newly written NTK covariance matrix contains a misindexed diagonal entry; the main regret bounds otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main nonlinear dueling-bandit, binary-feedback and RLHF contributions remain. The introduction drops the explicit 'first two' algorithm claim and newly emphasizes distinct arm-selection strategies and cross-entropy-specific confidence analysis as differences from prior approaches.

C2.justification: v2 adds computational tradeoffs, practical batching suggestions and an explanation of uninformative self-duels. It strengthens the effective-dimension comparison with a determinant-based argument. Appendix F explicitly leaves improved downstream LLM alignment unverified, qualifying the implications of its response-selection results.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly discloses retraining every 20 rounds with 50 gradient steps; this documents existing experiments rather than establishing a changed training schedule. Appendix F identifies embedding and reward-model provenance. Most architecture, regularization and hardware details were already present in v1 Appendix D.

R1.justification: The short related-work paragraph becomes a substantive Section 6 covering finite-armed, contextual and contextual dueling bandits, supplemented by Appendix C.2's strategy comparisons. References are expanded, including Filippi et al., Lin et al. (2024) and Dwaracherla et al.; Saha and Ghoshal (2022) is removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: detailed binary-feedback and RLHF sections move to appendices, concise implications remain in the main text, and substantial proof-sketch and related-work sections are introduced. The title, introductory explanations, headings and citation style are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 9, promotes the hyperparameter and NDB-TS sensitivity figures into the main text, and relocates binary-feedback displays into Appendix D. ICLR styling and some captions change, while the original eight figures retain their plots and panel structures.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited net gain through clearer proof exposition, training disclosures and an applied response-selection experiment beyond v1's synthetic studies. The gains are constrained by simulated preferences, untested downstream alignment and Figure 9's overstated NDB-TS interpretation. The added determinant-proportionality argument and misindexed NTK covariance also need correction, preventing a stronger quality assessment.
